svg.title: How the standby decides
svg.desc: Solana Validator Failover v0.7.0 on Alpenglow. The holder’s local self-fence threshold is 30 seconds by default. The standby has its own 60-second delay starting at first detected delinquency. Observed votes or lost visibility can restart it. The standby needs seven of the last ten local checks to show delinquency by default. It tries the preferred external RPC, with public fallback only if needed, and requires both external confirmation and a clear final local view. An explicit not-delinquent verdict resets the local window. Missing evidence or a veto holds the decision. A held episode alerts after 300 seconds by default. An unarmed standby alerts for a manual warm swap. An armed standby needs a 200-slot default readiness margin. With DRY_RUN it reports a simulated take. Otherwise it can perform a live cold take. The primary never automatically re-takes the identity.
